script:
Most of the IPL's biggest buys don't even beat an average player.
Every auction, two teams go to war over one name!
Twenty-five crore. Twenty-six. Twenty-seven.
Sold!
In 2025, Rishabh Pant went for twenty-seven crore. He scored 269 runs.
A year earlier, Shashank Singh cost twenty lakh. He scored 354.
Look at the three biggest buys from every auction since 2018. Only eight of twenty-six beat an average player.
Cheaper buys? Nearly four in ten.
The biggest paddle doesn't buy the best player.
caption:
Is the most expensive buy at an IPL auction worth the money?

We took the three biggest buys at every IPL auction since 2018. 26 of them played, and 8 beat an average player: 31%. Of all the other players teams bought, nearly four in ten did.

Rishabh Pant went for ₹27 crore in 2025 and scored 269 runs. A year earlier, Shashank Singh cost ₹20 lakh and scored 354.

"Beat an average player" means wins added in the Fine Margins model, IPL auctions 2018 to 2026.

What's the worst big buy you remember?
